prompt: A human wizard in iridescent silver-grey robes caught mid-gesture, his body rendered as a chronophotographic multiple exposure: three or four overlapping translucent copies of the same figure fanned across the frame, each copy tinted a different arcane hue (cerulean, wine-purple, emerald, amber), as if a single motion were strobe-frozen into many selves at once. His raised hand smears into a trail of afterimages. The background is a dim stone wizard sanctum lit by a cold prismatic glow. The only source of light is the shifting quicksilver shimmer around him.

A human wizard standing in three-quarter view, his own face a smooth blank silver mask reflecting nothing, while six different theatre masks orbit his head in a ring — each a distinct face (laughing, weeping, snarling, serene, cunning, hollow) and each a different color. One hand lifts a mask toward his blank face as if about to put it on, another mask falling away from the other hand. He wears quicksilver-grey robes. The background is a dim candlelit stagehouse with heavy velvet curtains. The masks glint as the only bright elements.

A humanoid figure made entirely of liquid mercury, a wizard mid-reformation: his lower body still a pool and rivulets of beading quicksilver flowing upward into a half-formed torso and arm, his face not yet settled, surface features sliding and rippling like mercury refusing to hold one shape. Mirror-bright droplets scatter and float around him catching colored light. He stands on dark polished stone. The background is a shadowed arcane vault, the only light a cold prismatic sheen rippling across his liquid-metal surface.

A human wizard in quicksilver-grey robes stands in side profile before a fan of upright mirror shards arranged like a folding screen. In each mirror shard his reflection is a DIFFERENT version of himself — one a fierce warrior-mage in red, one a hooded scholar in blue, one a serene healer in white, one a sinister figure in violet — each reflection in a different pose and color, none matching his actual stance. He touches one shard with a fingertip. The background is a dim panelled study. The mirrors are the brightest elements, each glowing its own hue.

A human wizard whose single body refracts through a prism into a spectral fan: his form disperses into offset copies trailing sideways across the frame, each copy a pure spectrum color (red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, violet) like chromatic aberration splitting one figure into many. His outline is silver where the colors converge. He raises both arms and the dispersion spreads from the gesture. The background is a dark obsidian chamber. The only light is the prismatic spectrum radiating from his fragmenting form.

The same human wizard repeated five times across the frame, identical face and pose but each rendered in a different arcane hue — cerulean, wine-purple, silver-grey, emerald, amber-gold — overlapping translucently like a chronophotographic multiple exposure of one man caught becoming many possible selves. The central silver-grey copy is the most solid; the colored copies grow fainter toward the edges. The background is a dim stone wizard sanctum. The only source of light is the shifting quicksilver shimmer around the figures.

A human wizard in quicksilver-grey robes seen from the front, his face a smooth featureless mirror-silver mask reflecting cold light, six distinct theatre masks orbiting his head in a wide ring — a laughing mask, a weeping mask, a snarling mask, a serene mask, a cunning mask, a hollow-eyed mask — each a different color (gold, blue, red, green, violet, white). His hands are clearly raised, one offering a mask up toward his blank face. The background is a dim candlelit stagehouse with deep red velvet curtains. The colored masks glint as the brightest elements.

The same young human wizard repeated five times across the frame, identical pose and clean-shaven face, each copy rendered in a different vivid arcane hue — cerulean blue, wine-purple, silver-grey, emerald green, amber-gold — overlapping translucently like a chronophotographic multiple exposure of one man caught mid-shift becoming many possible selves. The central silver-grey copy is solid and sharp; the colored copies grow ghostly and fainter toward the edges, their edges bleeding into quicksilver shimmer. The background is a dim stone wizard sanctum. The only light is the prismatic glow radiating off the figures.

A human wizard in quicksilver-grey robes facing forward, his own face a smooth blank mirror-silver mask, and SIX classical theatre masks floating in a full ring around his head and shoulders — comedy laughing, tragedy weeping, snarling, serene, sly, and hollow — each mask a different color: gold, blue, red, green, violet, white. His hands lift two of the masks. The masks are the bright focal elements. The background is a dim candlelit theatre with deep crimson velvet curtains framing both sides.
